issues.title: Inconsistent spacing around function arguments
issues.description: The code contains inconsistent spacing around commas in function arguments that violates the project's rustfmt configuration. Specifically, missing space after comma and extra spaces after comma in method calls.
issues.rule_name: Rust Code Must Be Formatted According to Project rustfmt Configuration

issues.title: Cookie deletion incorrectly calls SetCookie instead of DeleteCookie
issues.description: The delete_cookie function is sending a WebviewMessage::SetCookie message instead of WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie. This causes the cookie to be set/updated instead of being deleted when the delete_cookie API is called. Any code attempting to delete cookies will fail to remove them, and may inadvertently persist or update cookies that should be removed. This breaks the entire cookie deletion functionality and creates a security concern where sensitive cookies cannot be properly removed.

issues.title: Window size applied before position in window_features causing incorrect window placement
issues.description: In the window_features method, the size configuration is now applied before the position configuration, reversing the original order. This can lead to incorrect window positioning behavior because some window managers calculate the final window position based on the current window size. When the size is set after the position, the position may be recalculated or adjusted incorrectly. This particularly affects windows opened through the on_new_window handler when both size and position are specified in NewWindowFeatures.

issues.title: Changed window naming pattern breaks window label consistency
issues.description: The window label format for dynamically created windows has been changed from "new-{number}" to "new-window-{number}". This breaks the established naming convention and will cause any code that attempts to retrieve or manipulate these windows using the expected label format to fail. For example, code trying to access "new-0" or "new-1" will not find the windows, as they are now named "new-window-0" and "new-window-1". This affects window management, event handling, and any window lookup operations that depend on the label pattern.

issues.title: Public re-export lacks rustdoc documentation
issues.description: A new public API item (`pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;`) was added without a `///` documentation comment. Line comments (`// ...`) do not satisfy the rule requiring rustdoc comments for public APIs.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Remove this re-export in v3
pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;
issues.rule_name: Public APIs Must Include Documentation Comments

issues.title: New code uses unwrap() on fallible operations
issues.description: Added code introduces multiple `unwrap()` calls on fallible operations (`parse().unwrap()`, `set_title(...).unwrap()`, and `build().unwrap()`), which violates the rule prohibiting panics/unwraps in favor of explicit error handling via `Result`.
issues.rule_name: Functions Should Return Result Types for Fallible Operations

issues.title: User-facing API change without a .changes entry
issues.description: This PR changes a user-facing API (renaming/replacing `with_window_features` with `window_features` and updating docs/examples accordingly) but does not add any markdown change file under `.changes/` in the diff, violating the requirement to include a covector change file for releasable functionality/API changes.
issues.rule_name: Changes Requiring a Version Bump Must Include a Change File

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14020 - fix: a few regressions from previous PRs
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
The PR does three things: it restores the public `tauri::webview::Cookie` re-export and removes the redundant `cookie::Cookie` import, renames `WebviewWindowBuilder::with_window_features` to `window_features` (and reorders its size/position handling), and moves the API example's `on_new_window` handler under the desktop-only cfg block with a new window label. The re-export and example changes look correct. The rename is safe because `on_new_window` is still an unreleased feature listed in `.changes/on_new_window.md`.

However, the change to `WryWebviewDispatcher::delete_cookie` is wrong. The diff replaces `DeleteCookie` with `SetCookie` in `delete_cookie`, so deleting a cookie from a webview now sets it instead. This is a new regression introduced by a PR that claims to fix regressions, and it has no test to catch it. The `window_features` body also has rustfmt-breaking spacing. The verdict is request_changes because of the delete_cookie bug.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `delete_cookie` dispatch now sends `WebviewMessage::SetCookie` (crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs:1718), so `Webview::delete_cookie` / `WebviewWindow::delete_cookie` silently set the cookie instead of deleting it. That is a functional regression in a PR whose purpose is fixing regressions. It must be fixed before merge. The remaining issues (formatting and an unrelated label change) are minor.

architecture.overview:
Tauri's public `Webview` and `WebviewWindow` types forward cookie operations (`set_cookie`, `delete_cookie`, `cookies`) through the `tauri-runtime` `WebviewDispatch` trait. In the wry runtime, `WryWebviewDispatcher` wraps each call in a `WebviewMessage` and sends it over the event loop proxy via `send_user_message`. The event loop handler then calls the wry webview's cookie methods. Separately, `WebviewWindowBuilder` consumes `NewWindowFeatures` from `on_new_window` callbacks to configure the child window's size and position, plus platform-specific opener state.

This PR changes three areas. It restores a public `tauri::webview::Cookie` alias for `tauri_runtime::Cookie`, which is the same type as `cookie::Cookie`, so the public signatures stay the same. It renames `with_window_features` to `window_features`, which is safe because the feature is unreleased. And it moves the API example's `on_new_window` setup into the desktop-only block. The delete path, however, now dispatches the wrong message variant.
steps: Entry point: user code calls `Webview::set_cookie` / `delete_cookie` (crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs ~2084-2100), which forwards to the runtime dispatcher.

Runtime bridge: `WryWebviewDispatcher::delete_cookie` (crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs ~1712-1720) builds a `Message::Webview` carrying a `WebviewMessage`. This PR changes its variant to `SetCookie`, which is the bug.
Event loop: the handler at crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs ~3731-3740 matches `SetCookie` and `DeleteCookie` separately. After this PR, nothing constructs `DeleteCookie`.
Re-export: `tauri::webview::Cookie` (crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs:23) is now a public alias of `tauri_runtime::Cookie`, replacing the private `use cookie::Cookie`.

Window features: `WebviewWindowBuilder::window_features` (crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs ~1315) applies size, then position, then platform opener configuration to the builder. The new name is used in the docs and in the API example's `on_new_window` callback.

findings.title: delete_cookie dispatches SetCookie instead of DeleteCookie
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-runtime-wry/src/lib.rs`, `WryWebviewDispatcher::delete_cookie` (around lines 1712-1720) sends `WebviewMessage::SetCookie(...)`. It must send `WebviewMessage::DeleteCookie(cookie.into_owned())` so that `Webview::delete_cookie` removes the cookie. `set_cookie` on the line above should keep `SetCookie`. Confirm that the `DeleteCookie` variant is constructed again and that no dead-code warning remains. Optionally add a regression test in the wry or runtime tests that asserts `delete_cookie` sends the delete message. Keep the change to that one line.

findings.title: window_features spacing violates rustfmt and swaps size/position order
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs`, the `window_features` method (around lines 1315-1322) has formatting that rustfmt would reject: `inner_size(size.width,    size.height)` has extra spaces, and `position(position.x,position.y)` is missing a space after the comma. Fix the spacing to standard rustfmt output. Restore the original ordering (position before size) from the previous `with_window_features` implementation, unless there is a reason for the change, and say so in the commit message. Run `cargo fmt --check` on the crate to confirm.

findings.title: Unrelated window label change in API example
findings.body:
The PR's description lists three items: removing a redundant clone, restoring the `Cookie` re-export, and gating `on_new_window` to desktop. The example's child window label also changed from `new-{number}` to `new-window-{number}`. That change isn't mentioned and isn't needed for the fix. Unless it is intentional, it should be reverted or called out in the description, because the label is user-visible in the example.

::diff{file="examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs" lines="74-103"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, the `on_new_window` handler (around line 91) changed the child window label from `format!("new-{number}")` to `format!("new-window-{number}")`. This change is not part of the PR's stated goals. Revert it to `new-{number}`, unless it is intentional, in which case mention it in the PR description. Keep the rest of the desktop-only restructuring as is.

findings.title: Re-export restores the public Cookie type without changing signatures
findings.body:
`pub use tauri_runtime::Cookie;` in `crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs` replaces the private `use cookie::Cookie;`. `tauri_runtime::Cookie` is itself `pub use cookie::Cookie`, so this is the same type and the `set_cookie` / `delete_cookie` signatures stay compatible. The `// Remove this re-export in v3` note is a useful marker for the planned cleanup.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/src/webview/mod.rs" lines="20-24"}

findings.title: Desktop-only on_new_window setup keeps mobile builds clean
findings.body:
Moving the `app_` clone, the `AtomicUsize` counter, and `on_new_window` into the `#[cfg(all(desktop, not(test)))]` block means mobile and test builds no longer create unused variables or call an API they don't support. The `AtomicUsize` import became a full path, so the top-level import is no longer needed. The `window_features` method is gated on a platform list that matches `desktop`.

::diff{file="examples/api/src-tauri/src/lib.rs" lines="69-103"}

findings.title: Rename to window_features is safe because the feature is unreleased
findings.body:
Renaming `with_window_features` to `window_features` is a public API change on paper. But the method was added with `on_new_window` in the pending `.changes/on_new_window.md` entry (minor feat, not released; crate version is 2.7.0), so no shipped user depends on the old name. The rename is applied consistently to the method, its doc example in `webview_window.rs`, the `mod.rs` doc example, and the API example. No remaining references to `with_window_features` were found in the repo.

::diff{file="crates/tauri/src/webview/webview_window.rs" lines="1315-1315"}
